verdict.rationale: Activepieces documents a built-in MCP server that Claude, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client can connect to in order to build, test and drive flows (docs-4, docs-27, probe-4). Its embeddable MCP gives a backend a token to run a user's automations through AI (docs-13, docs-35), so an external agent can call workflows. The evidence leans toward platform management, though, rather than explicitly publishing each flow or connected-app action as its own MCP tool. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of exposing individual flows or piece actions as named MCP tools with defined schemas, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
